extracted.intended_audience: senior intelligence community officials, agency policymakers, and OMB/policy staff
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and responding to OMB Circular A-76 (performance of commercial activities) as it affects intelligence community operations, including whether activities should be contracted or retained in-house given security and mission constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 prohibition on in-house justification (strike/classified)
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular policy that 'activities may not be justified for in-house operation on the basis that (1) there is a possibility of a strike by contract employees, [or] (2) the activity involves or supports a classified program.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit A-76 rule cited in the memo; it prevents agencies from using the risk of contractor strike or the classified nature of an activity as permitted reasons to retain in-house operation under the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 does not recognize security reasons as justification for government operation
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 ... does not recognize security reasons as a justification for government operation of a facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo emphasizes that because A-76 does not admit security as a valid justification for in-house work, its application can force contracting of operations that are unacceptable for security-sensitive missions. Example given: Department of Energy's proposal to contract its all-source communications center was consistent with A-76 yet unacceptable to intelligence users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess public exposure and lack of flexibility impact on protecting sensitive intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: The public exposure and lack of flexibility inherent in the program mandated by the circular would not permit us to adequately protect sensitive intelligence material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating whether to apply A-76 procedures, agencies must examine whether the public competitive process and associated disclosure/flexibility constraints would jeopardize protection of intelligence sources and methods. If public exposure materially risks sensitive material, retention or exemption should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder acceptability of contractor operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Users of a facility (e.g., intelligence consumers) may find contractor operation unacceptable — illustrated by the Department of Energy case where 'users of the communications center, including the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), ... notified the Department of Energy that they would discontinue electrical transmission of intelligence to the Department of Energy if contractors operated the facility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should include whether operational partners or users would accept contractor operation; if critical data flows or cooperation would be cut off by contracting, in-house operation or exemption is indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for Intelligence Community-wide exemption and consistent standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone in the Intelligence Community shares the responsibility to protect intelligence sources and methods, and we should adopt a consistent community-wide position on what would or would not permit us to fulfill that responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo urges coordination across the Intelligence Community to seek a common exemption or uniform criteria for when A-76 should not apply, rather than leaving agencies subject to inconsistent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance private-sector use with mission security (practicality/economy/appropriateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Like the CIA, the National Security Agency relies on the private sector to provide goods and services whenever practical, economical, and appropriate. We endorse the general policies espoused in OMB Circular A-76 ... However, the public exposure and lack of flexibility inherent in the program ... would not permit us to adequately protect sensitive intelligence material. We must seek relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation criteria should include practicality, economy, and appropriateness of contracting, but these must be weighed against mission-security impacts; agencies should document where contracting is appropriate and where security concerns require in-house operation or formal exemption.
